title: Precision-gated traffic splitter for progressive model validation and automatic rollback
creator: Liang Chen
description:
Goal: Build a developer-friendly A/B/Canary controller that performs ultra-fine-grained progressive validation of model variants using precision traffic gates (micro-exposures), request-level shadow comparisons, and multi-metric sequential hypothesis checks that can trigger safe automatic rollback.

Scope and constraints:
- Controller surface: API + Console UX + control-plane runtime integration with serving routing.
- Exposes an experiment spec that app teams can set: traffic schedule (micro-step increments), metric suite, statistical test config (frequentist sequential or Bayesian), reconciliation window for shadow traffic, and rollback policy.
- Must integrate with existing telemetry (per-route cost/latency traces, token-level logs, and Eval harness signals).
- Non-goal: full experiment analytics UI (we will link to existing dashboards); focus is on rollout/decision automation and clear hooks for observability.

Why this approach: Current canaries are too coarse (few percent jumps) and rely on manual review of many metrics. For high-value model upgrades we need a mechanism that: (a) minimizes user exposure while gathering statistically meaningful signals, (b) allows multi-metric safety decisions that combine perf/cost/quality/safety, and (c) can act automatically when a regression is confidently observed. Precision gates (micro-exposures, e.g., 0.05% -> 0.2% -> 1% -> 5%) let us collect early signal without impacting downstream UX or costs. Shadow comparisons provide per-request semantic deltas for offline signals that complement online metrics.
acceptance_criteria:
1) API that accepts an experiment spec with: target_variant, baseline_variant, micro_exposure_steps (list), metrics_to_monitor (list), sequential_test_config (type, alpha/beta/thresholds), and rollback_policy (composite thresholds).
2) Runtime can apply split routing at 0.01% resolution and schedule automatic step-ups on passing checks.
3) Shadow path implemented: requests routed in parallel to candidate model with request ids preserved; differences stored in reconciliation table for at least 72h.
4) Built-in default metric suite: p95 latency, error rate, cost-per-request, automated-eval-quality (synthetic prompts), and safety_flag_rate. Console shows current step and composite test score.
5) Automatic rollback triggers when the sequential test rejects the null for regression on any high-priority metric OR composite score exceeds policy for sustained N evaluation windows (configurable).
6) Telemetry: per-step sample sizes, test statistics, and decision history logged to the audit trail and surfaced in the model-rollout dashboard.
7) Unit and integration tests for routing, scheduling, and rollback behaviors and a staging end-to-end run with a canary model (ENG-22110) that demonstrates rollback on synthetic regressions.
release_notes: Introduces precision-gated rollout controller (API + Console) with shadow traffic reconciliation and an automatic rollback engine based on sequential statistical checks. Defaults are conservative and require explicit opt-in for aggressive policies.
implementation_notes:
- Routing integration: extend smart routing layer with micro-split token to support sequential gate state keyed by experiment id.
- Stats engine: add an online sequential test implementation (choice between Bayesian posterior odds and frequentist sequential probability ratio test) as a pluggable module.
- Shadow path: non-blocking fork with separate throttles and scrubbed logs for PII.
- Decision composite: weighted scoring across metrics; weights configurable per experiment.
- Safeguards: manual pause, forced rollback, and emergency freeze hooks exposed to on-call.
- Backwards compatibility: if experiment spec omitted, behavior defaults to current coarse canary semantics.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Spurious rollbacks due to noisy metrics at tiny sample sizes. Mitigation: require sequential tests with explicit minimum sample constraints and smoothing windows; require multi-window confirmation for rollback.
Risk: Shadow traffic increases cost. Mitigation: shrink reconciliation window, sample only a subset of requests for deep offline evals, and provide cost-estimate before starting experiment.
Risk: Complexity for end users. Mitigation: provide three opinionated templates (Conservative, Standard, Aggressive) in Console and sensible defaults in the API.
